problems.title: A shared base gives a diagonal division ratio
problems.question: O is the intersection of the diagonals of quadrilateral ABCD. Areas ABD and BCD are in ratio 9:16. Find AO:OC.
problems.idea: Both triangles have base BD, so their areas compare their distances to BD.
formulas: For points A,O,C on one line through BD, perpendicular distances to BD are proportional to AO and OC.
steps: Triangles ABD and BCD share base BD. Their height ratio is 9:16.
Because A,O,C are collinear and O lies on BD, those heights equal AO·|sinθ| and OC·|sinθ| for the same angle θ.
Cancel the common factor to obtain AO:OC=9:16.

problems.title: Alternate side midpoints of a dodecagon
problems.question: Join the midpoints of alternate sides of a regular dodecagon, whose side is 4/(2+√3). Find the side of the resulting regular hexagon.
problems.idea: The midpoints lie on the dodecagon incircle.
formulas: Dodecagon apothem r=s/[2tan15°], with tan15°=2-√3; a regular hexagon side equals its circumradius.
steps: The apothem is s(2+√3)/2.
Substitute s=4/(2+√3) to get r=2.
Alternate side midpoints are 60° apart on this radius-2 circle, giving a regular hexagon of side 2.

problems.title: Semicircle inscribed in a 13-14-15 triangle
problems.question: A semicircle inscribed in ABC has its centre on AC. AB=13,BC=15,AC=14. Find the semicircular arc length.
problems.idea: Its centre lies where the B-angle bisector meets AC.
formulas: Angle-bisector theorem; Heron’s formula; area=side·distance/2; semicircular arc=πr.
steps: The semiperimeter is 21, so triangle area=√(21·8·6·7)=84.
If the centre is D on AC, then AD:DC=13:15, giving AD=14·13/28=6.5.
Area ABD=(6.5/14)·84=39. Its altitude from D to AB is the radius r, so 39=13r/2 and r=6.
The semicircular arc length is πr=6π.

problems.title: A section vector with one reversed side direction
problems.question: In ABC, BA=a and CB=b as vectors. D lies on AC with AD:DC=1:3. Find BD.
problems.idea: Use B as origin, noting that BC=-b.
steps: With B=0, A=a and C=-b.
Therefore D=(3a-b)/4.
Since B is the origin, this is vector BD.

problems.title: Same-sign expressions with an eighth root
problems.question: For which a do $(|a|-5)/(-a^2+2a-6)$ and $\sqrt[8]{a-3}/(a-2)$ have the same sign?
problems.idea: First restrict the domain of the even root.
steps: The second expression requires a≥3. It equals zero at 3 and is positive for a>3.
At a=3 the first is positive, so their signs differ.
For a>3, |a|=a. The first expression is positive exactly when a-5<0.
Thus both are positive for 3<a<5; at 5 the first is zero and the second positive.

problems.title: A term compared with its infinite tail
problems.question: Each nonzero term of a convergent infinite geometric progression is in ratio 2:3 to the sum of all its following terms. Find the common ratio.
problems.idea: Write the tail as a geometric series relative to that term.
steps: The ratio t:[tq/(1-q)]=2:3 gives (1-q)/q=2/3.
Thus 3-3q=2q, so q=3/5.
This lies inside (-1,1), so the infinite tail converges.

problems.title: Cube-root cancellation before a negative power
problems.question: Evaluate $[(\sqrt[3]a+\sqrt[3]{2b})/\sqrt[3]{4b^2}-1/\sqrt[3]{2b}]^{-3}$ for $a=2\sqrt3,b=\sqrt[4]3$.
problems.idea: Use u=∛a and v=∛(2b).
steps: The bracket becomes (u+v)/v²-v/v²=u/v².
Its negative cube is (2b)²/a=4b²/a.
Since b²=√3 and a=2√3, the value is 2.

problems.title: Mean of evenly spaced inserted terms
problems.question: Five numbers are inserted between 2 and 3 so that all seven form an arithmetic progression. Find the mean of the inserted numbers.
problems.idea: The five inserted terms are symmetric about the endpoint average.
formulas: The mean of an arithmetic progression is the average of its first and last terms.
steps: The common difference is (3-2)/6=1/6.
The inserted endpoints are 13/6 and 17/6.
Their average is (13/6+17/6)/2=5/2.

problems.title: Maximize a quadratic in the common difference
problems.question: An arithmetic progression has a₆=6. For which d is a₇a₅+a₇a₃+a₅a₃ greatest?
problems.idea: Express the neighbouring terms through a₆ and complete the square.
steps: The expression is (6+d)(6-d)+[(6+d)+(6-d)](6-3d).
This simplifies to 108-36d-d².
Complete the square: 432-(d+18)².
It is greatest when d+18=0.

problems.title: Equal index sums give equal geometric products
problems.question: In a geometric progression, b₁b₅b₉b₁₃=199. Find the geometric mean of b₂,b₆,b₈,b₁₂.
problems.idea: The two products have the same total exponent of the common ratio.
formulas: bₙ=b₁qⁿ⁻¹; the geometric mean of four positive values is their product’s fourth root.
steps: The first product is b₁⁴q^(0+4+8+12)=b₁⁴q²⁴.
The second product is b₁⁴q^(1+5+7+11)=b₁⁴q²⁴, so it is also 199.
Thus the requested geometric mean is ⁴√199.
problems.answer: $\sqrt[4]{199}$, under the usual positive-term convention for a geometric mean.

problems.title: A product inequality with an even root
problems.question: Solve $(x+3)\sqrt[6]{(6-x)/(8-x)}\ge0$.
problems.idea: Find the radical’s domain, then use its nonnegative sign.
formulas: An even root requires (6-x)/(8-x)≥0 and x≠8.
steps: The domain is x≤6 or x>8. The root is positive except at x=6, where it is zero.
Where the root is positive, require x+3≥0, or x≥-3.
The zero point x=6 is included.
Intersecting gives [-3,6]∪(8,∞).

problems.title: Isosceles triangle from an inradius and a half-angle
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has apex angle α, inradius 3 cm and tan(α/2)=3/4. Find its area.
problems.idea: Use a 3-4-5 half-triangle ratio.
steps: If each equal side is s, the half-base is 3s/5 and the altitude 4s/5.
The area is (3s/5)(4s/5)=12s²/25; the semiperimeter is s+3s/5=8s/5.
The area is 12·100/25=48.

problems.title: Overlap of two perpendicular rhombi
problems.question: A rhombus has diagonals 2 and 2√3. Rotate it 90° about their intersection. Find the overlap area.
problems.idea: In one quadrant the two diamond inequalities cut out a simple quadrilateral.
formulas: A centred rhombus with half-diagonals a,b satisfies |x|/a+|y|/b≤1.
steps: Take the original half-diagonals as 1,√3. The rotated inequalities in the first quadrant are x+y/√3≤1 and x/√3+y≤1.
The slanted boundaries meet at x=y=t, with t=√3/(√3+1)=(3-√3)/2.
The first-quadrant overlap has vertices (0,0),(1,0),(t,t),(0,1). Its area is t, by splitting into two triangles.
Multiply by four: area=4t=6-2√3.

problems.title: A parallel through the altitude midpoint
problems.question: In an isosceles triangle, a line parallel to an equal side passes through the midpoint of the altitude to the base. In what ratio does it divide the area?
problems.idea: Locate the smaller similar triangle cut off at a base vertex.
steps: Put the base endpoints at (-b,0),(b,0) and apex at (0,h). The altitude midpoint is (0,h/2).
The parallel line meets the base at (-b/2,0) and the other equal side at (b/4,3h/4).
The triangle at the right base vertex is similar to the original with side ratio 3/4, so it has 9/16 of the whole area.
The remaining piece has 7/16, giving ratio 9:7, or 7:9 when listed in the reverse order.

problems.title: Orthogonality determines a unit-vector angle
problems.question: Unit vectors a,b satisfy (2a+3b)⊥(-8a+7b). Find the angle between a and b.
problems.idea: Expand the zero dot product and use a·b=cosθ.
formulas: a·a=b·b=1; perpendicular vectors have dot product zero.
steps: Expansion gives -16+14(a·b)-24(a·b)+21=0.
Thus 5-10cosθ=0, so cosθ=1/2.
For an angle between vectors in [0°,180°], θ=60°.

problems.title: Count two-digit numbers with digit sum five
problems.question: Choose a two-digit positive integer uniformly. Find the probability that its digits sum to 5.
problems.idea: List the favourable numbers and count all two-digit numbers.
steps: The possible numbers are 14,23,32,41,50: five outcomes.
There are 99-10+1=90 two-digit numbers.
The probability is 5/90=1/18.

problems.title: How a trapezoid midline divides area
problems.question: A diagonal divides a trapezoid’s area in ratio 3:5. In what ratio does the midline divide its area?
problems.idea: The diagonal area ratio gives the base ratio.
formulas: A trapezoid diagonal gives triangles with the same height and bases equal to the two parallel bases.
steps: Write the bases as 3t and 5t. Their midline is 4t.
The two strips have equal height h/2.
Their areas are proportional to base sums 3t+4t=7t and 4t+5t=9t.
Thus the ratio is 7:9.

problems.title: Gap between three tangent equal circles
problems.question: Three circles of radius 3 cm touch externally in pairs. Find the curved triangular gap between them.
problems.idea: Subtract three 60° sectors from the equilateral triangle of centres.
formulas: Centre triangle side=2r; equilateral area=s²√3/4; sector area=(θ/360°)πr².
steps: The centres form an equilateral triangle of side 6, with area 9√3.
Each circle occupies a 60° sector inside it, of area 9π/6.
The three sectors total 9π/2.
The gap area is 9√3-9π/2.

problems.title: A changed exponent changes the radical result
problems.question: Evaluate $\sqrt[6]{3^8\cdot4^5}\sqrt[3]{3^5\cdot4}$.
problems.idea: Put both radicals under a sixth root.
steps: The product is ⁶√(3¹⁸·4⁷).
Extract the sixth powers 3¹⁸ and 4⁶ to obtain 27·4·⁶√4.
Since ⁶√4=∛2, the result is 108∛2.

problems.title: An even shifted power gives a vertical symmetry axis
problems.question: Find the symmetry axis of y=5-3/(x+2)¹⁶.
problems.idea: The expression is unchanged when x+2 changes sign.
steps: The inputs x=-2+t and x=-2-t give the same denominator t¹⁶.
Thus the graph is reflected onto itself across x=-2.
The point x=-2 is excluded from the domain, but the vertical line is still its symmetry axis.

problems.title: Area scales by the square of a homothety factor
problems.question: A homothety with factor -1/3 maps ABC to A₁B₁C₁. Their areas sum to 80 cm². Find area ABC.
problems.idea: The negative factor reverses position but areas use its square.
steps: Let the original area be S. The image area is S/9.
Therefore S=72.

problems.title: Match two monotonicity intervals
problems.question: The increasing interval of f(x)=3x²+6x-5 equals the decreasing interval of g(x)=-2x²+ax+8. Find a.
problems.idea: For each parabola, find the vertex x-coordinate.
formulas: Vertex x=-B/(2A); an upward parabola increases to the right, while a downward parabola decreases to the right.
steps: The vertex of f is x=-6/6=-1, so its increasing interval starts at -1.
The vertex of g is x=a/4, so its decreasing interval starts there.
Matching endpoints gives a/4=-1, hence a=-4.

problems.title: Line joining two parabola intercepts
problems.question: Find the line through the y-intercept and x-axis tangency point of y=x²-6x+9.
problems.idea: Factor the parabola and read its two axis contacts.
steps: The y-intercept is (0,9).
The x-axis tangency point is (3,0).
The slope is (0-9)/(3-0)=-3, and the intercept is 9.

problems.title: Convert a fraction of a radian to degrees
problems.question: Convert 1/6 radian to degrees.
problems.idea: Use π radians=180°.
steps: Multiply (1/6)·180°/π.
The result is 30°/π, approximately 9.55°.
problems.note: The identical answer 30°/π appears twice among the printed choices; both duplicate choices are correct.

problems.title: Recover a radicand from its domain endpoints
problems.question: Find a if f(x)=√[x²+(a²-28a/5)x+15-a²] has domain (-∞,-2]∪[5,∞).
problems.idea: A monic quadratic nonnegative exactly outside those endpoints must have roots -2 and 5.
steps: Compare constant terms: 15-a²=-10, so a²=25 and a=±5.
Compare linear terms: a²-28a/5=-3.
At a=5, this is 25-28=-3. At a=-5 it is 25+28=53, which fails.
